bottom_line: Rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.96).
implications: Based on the per-protocol, as-treated analysis, rivaroxaban met noninferiority versus warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism (0.79 [0.66–0.96]). In the intention-to-treat analysis, noninferiority was met (0.88 [0.75–1.03]) but superiority was not (P = 0.12). Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding was similar (1.03 [0.96–1.11]), while intracranial hemorrhage (0.67 [0.47–0.93]) and fatal bleeding (0.50 [0.31–0.79]) were lower with rivaroxaban and hemoglobin decreases ≥2 g/dl (1.22 [1.03–1.44]) and transfusions (1.25 [1.01–1.55]) were higher.

major_points.text: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, event-driven trial.
major_points.quote:
ROCKET AF) was a multi-
      center, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy,
      event-driven trial

major_points.text: Patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation at moderate-to-high risk for stroke were randomized to rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (15 mg daily if creatinine clearance 30–49 ml/min) or dose-adjusted warfarin (INR 2.0–3.0).
major_points.quote:
Patients were randomly assigned to receive fixed-
      dose rivaroxaban (20 mg daily or 15 mg daily in
      patients with a creatinine clearance of 30 to 49 ml
      per minute) or adjusted-dose warfarin (target in-
      ternational normalized ratio [INR], 2.0 to 3.0).

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) or systemic embolism.
major_points.quote:
The primary efficacy end point was the compos-
      ite of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and sys-
      temic embolism.

major_points.text: Primary analysis was prespecified as per-protocol, as-treated during treatment (or within 2 days after discontinuation).
major_points.quote:
The primary analysis was prespecified to be performed in the
per-protocol population, which included all pa-
tients who received at least one dose of a study
drug, did not have a major protocol violation, and
were followed for events while receiving a study
drug or within 2 days after discontinuation

major_points.text: Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding was similar overall, with lower intracranial hemorrhage and fatal bleeding but more hemoglobin decreases ≥2 g/dl and transfusions with rivaroxaban.
major_points.quote:
Rates of intracranial hemor-
rhage were significantly lower in the rivaroxaban
group than in the warfarin group (0.5% vs. 0.7%
per year; hazard ratio, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.93;
P = 0.02).

analysis_methods.text: Estimated approximately 14,000 patients would need to be randomized based on projected warfarin event rate and annual attrition.
analysis_methods.quote:
On the
basis of a projected event rate of 2.3% per 100
patient-years in the warfarin group and a projected
14% rate of annual attrition, it was estimated that
approximately 14,000 patients would need to be
randomly assigned to a study group.

analysis_methods.text: Hazard ratios, confidence intervals, and P values calculated using Cox proportional-hazards models with treatment as the only covariate.
analysis_methods.quote:
Hazard ratios,
confidence intervals, and P values were calculated
with the use of Cox proportional-hazards mod-
els with treatment as the only covariate.

analysis_methods.text: Noninferiority tested at one-sided 0.025; superiority at two-sided 0.05.
analysis_methods.quote:
Testing
for noninferiority was based on a one-sided sig-
nificance level of 0.025; testing for superiority was
based on a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
